reason: core/src/semantic/call.rs's own module doc comment already named 'argument/result bindings' as part of the eventual CallFact contract (.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#callfact), but CallSiteIdentity never carried them -- a real, contract-named gap, not scope creep.

CALL and DATA_FLOW are two independent extraction passes over the same AST with no cross-reference between a call's argument expression and the DATA_FLOW Use it corresponds to, or between the call's result and the Definition/Store consuming it.

Closing this safely required proving CALL can independently compute the SAME record_id DATA_FLOW's own walker produces for a given argument -- not merely predicting it -- since a wrong prediction would repeat exactly the identity-invention mistake this whole R4 hardening arc has been fighting (the R4.9 OwnershipTarget bug, PERSISTENCE's PlaceRef guard, etc.).

design_decision.question: Can CALL reuse the existing PlaceRef bridge (core::semantic::persistence, R4.11) instead of inventing a new cross-reference mechanism?
design_decision.answer: YES. PlaceRef was already dimension-agnostic in shape (Resolved{dimension, record_id} | Unresolved); it had never had a second real consumer until now. Moved to its own module, core::semantic::place, once R4.12's CALL argument binding gave it that second consumer -- the right time to generalize, not before.
design_decision.convergence_mechanism: CallSiteIdentity.arguments[i] is computed by constructing the SAME ValueIdentity struct DATA_FLOW's own walker would build for that argument position (function/name/span/role, the only fields ValueIdentity::identity_key() actually uses) and calling identity_key() itself -- never a hand-duplicated copy of that formula. The recognition rule for 'is this argument expression a DATA_FLOW Use site' (spelling::simple_path_ident) was factored out of dataflow.rs and is now called by BOTH walkers, so they cannot silently drift apart.
design_decision.safety_gate: A Resolved reference is only ever constructed when SemanticDimension::DataFlow is part of the SAME extraction request (self.wants(DataFlow)) -- proven by call_argument_place_ref_stays_unresolved_when_data_flow_was_not_requested -- so CALL never names a record this exact request will not produce.

fix.what: CallSiteIdentity gained arguments: Vec<PlaceRef>, excluded from identity_key() (same precedent as dispatch/callees). adapter::semantic::rust::mod's Expr::Call/MethodCall arms compute one PlaceRef per syntactic argument via the new place_ref_for_argument helper.
fix.scope_this_wave: Argument binding ONLY. Result binding (the Definition/Store a call's return value flows into) remains explicit TARGET work: it requires threading enclosing-binding context through the CALL walker's statement-level traversal (knowing whether the call is the init of a simple let/assign), which argument binding did not need.
adversarial_coverage_added: call_argument_place_ref_converges_on_the_data_flow_uses_own_record_id (the convergence proof, mirroring R4.11's PlaceRef proof pattern)

new_interpretation: R4.5's CALL↔DATA_FLOW argument-binding gap is CLOSED. R4.5's overall closure status (macro-invocation-opacity gap, shared with every other full-expression-tree dimension) is otherwise unchanged. Result-binding remains a separate, still-open TARGET.
required_runtime_invariants: a simple single-identifier call argument's PlaceRef names the exact record_id DATA_FLOW's own Use observation for that argument carries
a call argument requiring deeper analysis (a method-call receiver, a nested call, a literal, ...) stays PlaceRef::Unresolved, never fabricated from spelling
a Resolved PlaceRef is only ever constructed when DataFlow was requested in the same extraction call
arguments never affect a call site's own identity_key()

self_census_cross_check.scale: 5260 real CALL observations in this repository's own source
self_census_cross_check.finding: 1045 arguments resolved to a real DATA_FLOW record_id, 3578 correctly stayed Unresolved (complex expressions) -- the feature fires genuinely on real code, not only test fixtures. exact_duplicates_merged remained 0 and conflict_candidates remained empty at this larger scale (25912 -> 26189 typed observations).
